title: Odysseys2: a long-horizon web agent benchmark
summary: CMU and Browser Use's long-horizon web agent benchmark. The best agent, GPT-6 Astra, fully completes 47 of 100 live-web tasks; mean rubric score 84.6/100.

Research


Odysseys2: a collaboration between Carnegie Mellon University and Browser Use


Odysseys2 is a long-horizon web agent benchmark from Carnegie Mellon University and Browser Use: 100 long tasks on the live web, each graded on 8 to 12 pass/fail checks. It builds on Carnegie Mellon University's[Odysseys](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24964) . The full paper-style write-up, with interactive charts and all 100 tasks, is at **[odysseysbench.com/v2](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/)** . This post is the short version.


## The result


The best agent fully completes 47 of 100 tasks.


GPT-6 Astra (default effort) has a mean rubric score of 84.6, yet falls short on the other 53.

Sorted by tasks fully completed, then mean score. Opus 5.5 is second with 18. Fable 5: content filters blocked 2 tasks, so its mean uses 98. Scores come from an LLM judge that has not been validated against a human reference.


15 agents, one 60-minute attempt per task, all in[BrowserCode](https://github.com/browser-use/browsercode) . Opus 5.5 is second with 18 fully completed. Five agents complete none.[Full leaderboard](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#results) .


## Fast is not good


Fig. 2


·


Score banked over time


At 15 minutes GPT-5.6 Luna has 37 points and Opus 5.5 has 18. By 60 minutes, Opus 5.5 and Grok 4.7 finish well above Luna.


Mean rubric score (0 to 100) from attempts finished by each minute, over all 100 attempts. BrowserCode harness, high effort, 1 dot per minute.


At 15 min: Luna 37


· Opus 5.5 18


· Grok 4.7 12


Grok 4.7 catches Luna at about 30 minutes and Opus 5.5 at about 36. An attempt adds its score when it finishes, not while it runs. Luna's line ends at 58.9, below its 59.7 mean, because one attempt has no recorded time.


At 15 minutes GPT-5.6 Luna leads with 37 points to Opus 5.5's 18. Opus catches up at about 36 minutes and ends at 71.2.[More](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#time) .


## The harness matters


Fig. 3


·


Same model, three harnesses


In the Python library Luna stays near 30. In BrowserCode it climbs to 63.0, in Pi to 71.9.


Mean rubric score, 0 to 100, for GPT-5.6 Luna on all 100 tasks, by reasoning effort. One run per setup. Python library has no max setting.


Harnesses hand the judge different records of the run, so these gaps mix differences in execution with differences in the evidence available for grading. Pi was tested with Luna only.


Same model, GPT-5.6 Luna: about 33 in the Browser Use Python library, 59 to 72 in BrowserCode and Pi at high to max effort.[More](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#sweep) .


## Grading changes scores


Fig. 4


·


Same attempts, two judges


Odysseys judge


Odysseys2 judge


Under the original judge every agent scores 77 to 96. Under the Odysseys2 judge the same attempts spread from 2 to 85.


Mean rubric score, 0 to 100, for 14 agents, each graded twice on the same saved attempts. Gemini 3.7 Flash: 94.9 vs 5.8.


The original Odysseys judge grades one check at a time from the action history and screenshots and does not see delivered files. The Odysseys2 judge also reads the files and zeroes flagged attempts. These differences measure disagreement between the judges; lower scores alone do not establish greater accuracy.


On the same attempts, the original Odysseys judge and the stricter Odysseys2 judge, which also reads the delivered files, disagree a lot: Gemini 3.7 Flash scores 94.9 under one and 5.8 under the other. That is disagreement, not proof of accuracy.[How tasks are built](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#tasks) ,[how grading works](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#grading) ,[the two judges](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#judges) .


## Limitations


The judge is not yet validated against a reliable human reference, reward-hacking flags are model judgments, and the live web changes. See[validating our judge](https://odysseysbench.com/v2/#people) for the full list.
